sections.h2: Whom do I call about a Hillsborough County property tax question?
sections.html:
It depends on the question. The Hillsborough County Property Appraiser handles value and exemptions. The Hillsborough County Tax Collector handles money, receipts and payment plans.

The appraiser's downtown Tampa office is on the 15th floor of the County Center, 601 E. Kennedy Boulevard, reachable at (813) 272-6100 Monday through Friday from 8 to 5. The collector publishes bills, payment options and a property search on its real estate tax page. A board separate from both offices, the Value Adjustment Board, hears value and exemption disputes.

  • Property Appraiser: just value, homestead filings, the assessment cap, portability and the TRIM notice.
  • Tax Collector: bills, installment applications, partial payments and tax certificates.
  • Clerk of the Circuit Court: recorded deeds, liens and the tax deed auction.

The appraiser's site also promotes a free Property Fraud Alert that flags new recordings made in your name. Heirs holding an empty Tampa Bay house are the people most likely to want it switched on.

sections.h2: How does a Hillsborough County bill and its early payment discount work?
sections.html:
Hillsborough tax notices land in November and can be paid from the 1st. The collector's FAQ says an account still open on April 1 picks up 3% interest and advertising costs.

Early payers get a cut of 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February, and March is full price. A winter seller should ask the closing agent which of those months the closing date falls in, since the sale proceeds may be what pays the bill.

Smaller checks are possible through the installment plan, which needs an application before May 1 and starts with a June payment. Paying in July keeps the plan alive but forfeits the discount. If nothing arrives by July 31 the account leaves the plan and the whole balance is payable the next November, with the 4 percent break. A separate partial payment option exists for current-year bills only, and an overdue real estate account has to be cleared in one payment.

The appraiser's home page reports that the latest TRIM mailing began August 13, with longer office hours, and links a 2026 Hurricane Damage Adjustment Form for storm-hit owners. A refused exemption produces an Official Notice of Denial by July 1, which opens a hearing before a Value Adjustment Board magistrate.

sections.h2: What exemptions can a Hillsborough County owner stack?
sections.html:
A permanent residence can shed up to $50,000 of assessed value in two layers.

Layer one touches every levy. Layer two sits on the slice of assessed value above $50,000 and skips school taxes. A yearly growth limit then applies after the first year. The appraiser accepts filings year round, cites March 1 as the legal deadline, and says a late one may still be taken up to 25 days after TRIM notices are mailed.

  • Low income senior: unincorporated Hillsborough County and the City of Tampa allow up to $50,000, and Temple Terrace allows up to $25,000.
  • Long term resident senior: Tampa and unincorporated areas, for homes with just value under $250,000 and 25 consecutive years in residence.
  • Veteran, disability, widow and blind exemptions: these need documents, and Hillsborough County Veterans Affairs lists 813-635-8316 for help with discharge papers.

Claiming homestead on a house you have left is expensive. According to the appraiser, the exempted taxes from the prior 10 years turn into a lien carrying a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest, so report a move-out before the sign goes in the yard.

sections.h2: What did Amendment 3 change for Hillsborough County homesteads?
sections.html:
Voters passed the statewide property tax amendment on November 3, 2026. A statement from the Hillsborough appraiser about its passage sits on that office's home page.

On its legislative update page the appraiser describes homestead exemption amounts of up to $150,000 from 2027 and up to $250,000 from 2028, with lawmakers told to schedule more increases. That page adds that the effect varies by parcel and cannot be calculated in advance. Treat the number on today's bill as the working figure until a TRIM notice shows a new one. The tax collector keeps a property tax reform page on the same ballot item.

Sellers feel this mostly through the buyer. The first bill after a purchase begins from just value, and a new exemption amount reaches the buyer only after an application is filed.

sections.h2: Who pays the tax when a Hillsborough County house closes?
sections.html:
An open Hillsborough County bill is settled out of the seller's proceeds at the table, because the lien stays with the land. The collector says the name printed on a bill is no obstacle to paying it, since a recorded deed may not have reached the appraiser before the roll was certified.

The seller's homestead ends with the sale, and the buyer starts over at just value after the next January 1 and files a new application. What the seller can carry along is the portable savings, which attach to a replacement home.

  • Escrowed loans: the servicer pays from a list it sends the collector, and once the loan is paid off the next bill is mailed to the owner.
  • Deed stamps: the state rate applies here because Hillsborough is not Miami-Dade, and each party on the deed shares the liability.
  • Portability: the replacement homestead has a three year window and needs a DR-501T with the new application.

sections.h2: How does unpaid Hillsborough County tax reach a tax deed sale?
sections.html:
A skipped bill becomes a tax certificate first, and a deed sale can come about two years after that.

The collector auctions certificates online. Bids start at 18 percent and fall by 0.25 percent per step, and the lowest bidder wins a certificate that ranks first among liens, including other government ones. Per the collector, a deed application cannot begin until up to 22 months after issue. The statute measures two years from April 1 of the issue year. When a homestead owes under $250, the county takes the certificate itself and no investor can buy it.

The clerk conducts the deed auction, and a homestead parcel's opening bid includes half of the last assessed value. An owner who is behind can still sell, since paying off the certificate at closing clears the title.

faqs.q: When is Hillsborough County property tax due?
faqs.a: Bills are payable November 1 and go delinquent April 1. The discount is 4 percent in November, then 3, 2 and 1 percent through February. An account open on April 1 picks up 3% interest and advertising costs.

faqs.q: Can I pay Hillsborough County tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, if you apply before May 1. The first payment is due in June, a July payment keeps you in the plan without the discount, and missing July 31 drops the account into a single November payment with the 4 percent discount.

faqs.q: Who decides a Hillsborough County homestead claim?
faqs.a: The Property Appraiser does. Filing closes March 1, any denial notice is mailed by July 1, and an appeal heads to the Value Adjustment Board. The collector never rules on eligibility.

faqs.q: Are partial payments allowed on a delinquent Hillsborough County bill?
faqs.a: No. Only current-year bills qualify for the partial plan, and an overdue real estate bill needs the full balance. Call the collector before sending anything smaller.

faqs.q: What if I sell before my Hillsborough County bill arrives?
faqs.a: The bill is still paid at closing. The title agent requests the amount from the collector and takes it out of the seller's money, and the buyer applies for a new homestead by the next March 1.
